title: Windows: double-clicking the app opens a console window beside it; the log should show only when started from a terminal

labels.name: in-review
labels.description: Fix pushed on a branch with an open PR; merges at the next cut

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Reported by the maintainer in chat (filed by an agent), 2026-11-12: "when double clickking the UI application, u get a terminal opening with some gpu information and stuff. That is not necessary to have visible in its own window. The UI should just open on its own and that terminal output only be visible if its started from a terminal."

**What happens.** On Windows the GUI binary (`crates/ui/src/main.rs`) is built as a console program (it has no `windows_subsystem` attribute), so Explorer gives it a new console window, which shows the start-up log (GPU adapter lines and the rest).

**Expected.**
- Started by double-click, from the Start menu or a shortcut: only the app window; no console window appears, not even for a moment.
- Started from a terminal (cmd, PowerShell, Windows Terminal, Git Bash): the same log lines appear in that terminal as today, and redirecting to a file or a pipe (`camcraft > log.txt 2>&1`) still works.
- Nothing is silenced: the Prime Directive says "Log diagnostics, never silence". If the log has no terminal to go to, it must still reach wherever the app already keeps its log (say where that is; if there is no log file today, say so in the PR and file the follow-up rather than adding one here).
- A crash or a start-up failure with no console must still be visible to the user (a message box or the existing error path), not a window that never appears.
- Linux and macOS behave as today; the headless `camcraft-cli` stays a console program.

**How (general Windows practice, no vendor code).** Build the GUI binary for the Windows subsystem (`#![cfg_attr(all(windows, not(debug_assertions)), windows_subsystem = "windows")]` or unconditionally) and, at start-up on Windows, attach to the parent's console when there is one (`AttachConsole(ATTACH_PARENT_PROCESS)`) and re-point stdout/stderr at it, leaving redirected handles alone. Keep the platform code in one small `#[cfg(windows)]` module (core code stays platform-neutral, AGENTS.md "Stays buildable everywhere"); no `unwrap`/`expect`; a failed attach is not an error. Prefer the `windows-sys` crate if it is already in the dependency tree; a NEW dependency needs the maintainer's yes (`needs-maintainer`).

Check the installer / release packaging and the UI test harness (`test_harness.rs`, `VisualRunner`) still capture output and that `cargo run` in a terminal still prints.

Done means: the release build opens with no console from Explorer and prints to the terminal it was started from; redirect works; a start-up failure is still shown; pinned as far as a test can (the subsystem of the built exe read from its PE header in an `xtask` or packaging check; the attach logic's pure part unit-tested); the PR body says what was checked by hand and what the maintainer must try (double-click, terminal, redirect).
